stories.title: "Jesus loves 'em": Man with cross offers a simple message
stories.summary: Durrell Bell felt called by God to carry a nearly 6-foot-5 wooden cross through storms and 70 miles of Washington roads. Five months in, he finished the journey from Longview to Olympia — and his message stayed simple: Jesus loves 'em.
stories.extended_summary: Wind tore through Lewis County hard enough to lift anything not bolted down — but Durrell Bell stayed planted, anchored by the weight of a nearly 6-foot-5 wooden cross on his shoulder. Five months ago, he felt compelled by God to start walking with it, first a few miles a week, then a calling he couldn't shake: 70 miles from Longview to Olympia. He walked 20 miles the first day, 17 the next, alone but never lonely — his wife Teyonna shuttled him each morning and night, and strangers fed him along the way. Etched into the cross's fibers are the names of everyone he's met. His message never got complicated: Jesus loves 'em.

Their mission: land, load the most critically wounded Marines, and get them to a hospital. One of those 12 was Evelyn Schretenthaler, a young woman from Zap, North Dakota. A new book, 'The Flight Nurses' War' by Leah Garrett, chronicles their story for the first time — the fear, the courage, and the thousands of lives they pulled out of the bloodiest battles in Marine Corps history.
